items.t: No City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood plan or official boundary document names a "Cottonwood" neighbourhood — the City publishes no boundary for it.
Maple Ridge's community-level attached median that month was $525,000; SnapStats publishes no Cottonwood-only median.

Where the attached stock concentrates: the Cottonwood Drive corridor (Cottonwood Drive addresses are classified Cottonwood MR in listing feeds, including addresses west of the Kanaka Creek core — that is the board's classification, not a City boundary), Kanaka Way, and the 236–240 Street blocks around the two elementary schools.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cottonwood MR condos

items.t: The area's name comes from a street, not a plan. Cottonwood Drive carries several of the complexes (Verigin's Ridge, Carriage Lane, Cottonwood Green), and the board applies the Cottonwood MR label along that corridor even west of Kanaka Creek — check the sub-area classification on the listing itself rather than assuming a City boundary.
One complex, two published build years. The strata plan and Form B settle the year.
The Fraserview Village 55+ buildings are not here.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Cottonwood MR
It is not Cottonwood Village in Chilliwack, which is a pad-rental manufactured-home park.
Streets, schools and transit near Cottonwood MR townhomes

items.t: The area's official anchors are Kanaka Creek Elementary at 11120 234A Street and Kanaka Creek, which runs through the area to the Fraser River; the residential area sits around Kanaka Creek Elementary (234A Street) and Alexander Robinson Elementary (238B Street), west of 240 Street and east of the Town Centre, with Kanaka Creek Regional Park along the creek.
Nearby areas: East Central and the Town Centre to the west, Albion to the east beyond 240 Street, Thornhill to the north.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Cottonwood Drive cluster (The Meadows at Verigin's Ridge, Cottonwood Terrace, Carriage Lane), Kanaka Way (Cottonwood Grove), 236 Street (Maplewood Creek), 240 Street (Willow & Oak), 119 Avenue (Hollyhock) and 112 Avenue (The Falls).
Maple Ridge is a SnapStats-covered community.

Schools physically inside the area: Kanaka Creek Elementary (K–7), 11120 234A Street, and Alexander Robinson Elementary (K–7), 11849 238B Street, at the north edge; no secondary school is inside Cottonwood MR, and SD42 has no middle tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12).

Transit: the bus route named for the area is the 745 Haney Place / Cottonwood on TransLink's Haney Place route diagram; the 746 Haney Place / Albion interlines with the 745 at Jackson Road at 103 Avenue, forming one circular service; no West Coast Express station is in Cottonwood MR.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Cottonwood MR

items.t: Strata vs fee-simple — the core distinction, applied honestly here: three counted complexes are confirmed strata (The Meadows expressly, Cottonwood Terrace and Carriage Lane on their directories' strata-bylaw records). A strata townhouse buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, and gets a Form B package. A fee-simple townhouse buyer owns the lot outright: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees — municipal rules and any registered covenants/HOA only.

Form B diligence (strata complexes): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata): since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote — the central check on the 1990s Cottonwood Drive stock (Cottonwood Terrace 1993, Hollyhock 1996, Carriage Lane 1998/1999). Since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.

Co-op contrast (St. George's Village): a co-op purchase is a share purchase with board approval and the co-op's own transfer fee — no Form B, no strata fees in the Strata Property Act sense, and financing is lender-specific. Do not run a strata checklist on a co-op unit.

What is settled: no Cottonwood-specific area plan exists, so the OCP's general policies govern this sub-area. Two dated plan facts nearby: the Albion Area Plan was adopted October 28, 2025 (Albion is east of 240 Street, outside this sub-area), and the Lougheed Transit Corridor plan south of the area was adopted January 27, 2026 per the City record (Council approved the OCP amendments January 27, 2026; OCP Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 given third reading and adoption January 27, 2026; the corridor ends at 221 Street) — an earlier contrary reading of that corridor's status is noted in.

Suites and SSMUH: one secondary suite per lot, inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area, building permit required; eligible single-detached and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH rules, subject to zoning, bylaw and building code requirements — relevant to Cottonwood's detached streets, not to its townhouse complexes.

Creek and flood: Kanaka Creek is a salmon-bearing watercourse through the area and the regional park protects the creek corridor; whether a specific Cottonwood MR lot is in a mapped floodplain is per-lot on the City flood maps at MapleRidge.ca/Flood.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cottonwood MR townhomes

items.t: The City does not use this neighbourhood's name at all: Maple Ridge's neighbourhoods page does not list Cottonwood, and no Cottonwood area plan exists — the board name survives in listings and SnapStats while the City and the school district anchor the area by Kanaka Creek and its two elementary schools. With no area plan, rezoning expectations should be set by the OCP's general policies, not neighbourhood-plan promises.

Two housing things here are both called Cottonwood Park / Cottonwood-something and are not housing you can buy: Cottonwood Park (11600 Cottonwood Dr) is income-based subsidized rental run by Red Door Housing Society, and Cottonwood North Park (12111 238B St) is a City picnic park. Neither is a townhouse complex.

The co-op at the north edge is easy to mistake for a strata: St. George's Village's homes are townhouses and its listings read like strata listings, but its own membership form gives it away — a 55-year age qualification for MEMBERSHIP, clear title to the land held by the co-op, and a $3,500 share-transfer fee. It also sits beside St George Maple Ridge Anglican church (23500 Dewdney Trunk Rd), which is the likely source of a stray "St. Andrew's" seniors name that matches nothing in Maple Ridge.

The creek is working salmon habitat, not just scenery: Kanaka Creek Regional Park's Bell-Irving Hatchery supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout, the Canyon Trail runs 1.2 km one way from the hatchery to Cliff Falls, and the Riverfront Trails run 3 km one way at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River — the amenity the Cottonwood Drive complexes back onto, and the reason creek setbacks bind.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cottonwood MR
Fee-simple lots

items.t: The stock: no Cottonwood area plan exists, so no City plan document sets out housing types for this area and city-wide housing rules apply; the residential streets around the two elementary schools are single-detached subdivisions under the RS zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019. The documented base is freehold houses, with secondary suites and SSMUH units as the added-density paths. Fee-simple is the default form: own title, no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.

Lot character, as the bylaw states it: the bylaw schedule gives a minimum lot area of 668 m² for RS-1; the other RS variants (RS-1a through RS-1d, RS-2, RS-3) carry their own schedules in the same bylaw, and the bylaw's residential zones also include RST, RT-1, RT-2 and RM-1 to RM-4.
Built strata ground is not land stock

blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: Tenure trap on the area's edge — not land stock: St. George's Village Seniors Housing Co-operative (23580 Dewdney Trunk Road, north edge) holds its land as a co-operative — its membership form states the co-op "has clear title to land" and members buy shares, not lots.

blocks.text: Servicing, ALR, creek and assemblies

items.t: No ALR split is stated.
No servicing claim is filled in.

Creek corridor is not buildable lot area: Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) follows Kanaka Creek through this part of Maple Ridge, with the Canyon Trail from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls (1.2 km one way) and Riverfront Trails (3 km one way) at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River; Metro Vancouver notes steep slippery cliffs along the creek, especially at Cliff Falls, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout. Lots backing onto the creek carry setback/slope diligence — price buildable area, not creek-front gross area.

Land assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals: none documented for Cottonwood MR — no assembly, development site or rezoning proposal is named, and none is presented as for-sale inventory. South of the area, the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan directs growth around future Bus Rapid Transit stations along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road — a plan for corridor ground to the south, not a Cottonwood MR lot offering (adoption position).

Market context, labelled correctly: Maple Ridge is a SnapStats-covered community, cited as community context only. SnapStats has no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined) — no detached figure is presented as a land figure.

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge. The City does not list Cottonwood as a named neighbourhood on its neighbourhoods page (which lists Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Ruskin, Silver Valley, Thornhill, Town Centre, Webster's Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon), and no Cottonwood area plan appears on the City's area plans list.

Main roads: Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road are the east–west corridors south and north of the area, and Haney Place in the Town Centre is the bus exchange the area's routes connect to; local streets named in TransLink routing include 232 Street, 238B Street, Kanaka Way, 240 Street and 104 Avenue.

Transit: the bus route named for this area is the 745 Haney Place / Cottonwood; the 746 Haney Place / Albion interlines with the 745 at Jackson Road at 103 Avenue, forming one circular service; no West Coast Express station is in Cottonwood MR — the nearest stations are in the Town Centre.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Cottonwood MR

items.t: OCP: sources differ on the OCP citation; confirm with the municipality.

Neighbouring plans, precisely placed: the Albion Area Plan was adopted October 28, 2025 — Albion is east beyond 240 Street, outside this sub-area. Its effect is on corridor/Town Centre land, not on Cottonwood lots directly.

SSMUH / suites as the City states them — Maple Ridge's own figures, not Abbotsford's: one secondary suite per lot, inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area, with a building permit required; eligible single-detached and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH rules, subject to zoning, bylaw and building code requirements.
Flood / watercourse: Kanaka Creek is a salmon-bearing watercourse through the area and the regional park protects the creek corridor.

ALR rules (where a parcel is confirmed ALR — none identified in Cottonwood MR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cottonwood MR lots

items.t: No recreation centre, library or shopping centre sits inside the sub-area: the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre is at 11925 Haney Place in the Town Centre, Maple Ridge Public Library is at 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, and the nearest Town Centre centres named in the City's downtown guide are Haney Place Mall, 11900 Haney Place, and Valley Fair Mall, 22709 Lougheed Highway. Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, provides 24/7 emergency services; the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is in Haney Place Mall, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

The bus is a loop, not a line: the 745 Cottonwood and 746 Albion interline at Jackson Road at 103 Avenue and run as one circular service to Haney Place Exchange, so trip time depends on which direction around the loop a lot's stop sits.

Two "Cottonwood Park" names, neither is buyable land: Cottonwood Park (11600 Cottonwood Drive) is subsidized non-profit rental run by Red Door Housing Society, and Cottonwood North Park (12111 238B Street) is a City picnic park — searches mix them up, and neither is a lot offering.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Cottonwood MR
The ground in Cottonwood MR

items.t: Parcel character: the bylaw schedule gives a minimum lot area of 668 m² for RS-1; the other RS variants (RS-1a through RS-1d, RS-2, RS-3) carry their own schedules in the same bylaw, whose residential zones also include RST, RT-1, RT-2 and RM-1 to RM-4. A 668 m² minimum is a house-lot figure, not an acreage figure.

Creek-corridor ground is amenity and constraint at once, not extra acreage: Kanaka Creek is a salmon-bearing watercourse through the area and the regional park protects the creek corridor; Metro Vancouver flags steep slippery cliffs along the creek at Cliff Falls. A lot backing onto the creek carries setbacks, slope and flood-map checks.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Cottonwood MR acreages

items.t: Municipality: City of Maple Ridge, BC. The City does not list Cottonwood as a named neighbourhood on its neighbourhoods page (that page lists Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Ruskin, Silver Valley, Thornhill, Town Centre, Webster's Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon), and no Cottonwood area plan appears on the City's area plans list.
The area's official anchors are Kanaka Creek Elementary at 11120 234A Street and Kanaka Creek, which runs through the area to the Fraser River.

Main roads and commute: Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road are the east–west corridors south and north of the area, and Haney Place in the Town Centre is the bus exchange the area's routes connect to; local streets named in TransLink routing for the area include 232 Street, 238B Street, Kanaka Way, 240 Street and 104 Avenue.

Parks and trails: Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) follows Kanaka Creek through this part of Maple Ridge, with trails for walking, cycling and horseback riding, the Canyon Trail from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls (1.2 km one way), Riverfront Trails (3 km one way) at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery supporting chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout; Metro Vancouver notes steep slippery cliffs along the creek, especially at Cliff Falls.

Recreation / library / shopping: no City recreation centre is located in Cottonwood MR (the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre is at 11925 Haney Place in the Town Centre); no library branch sits in Cottonwood MR (Maple Ridge Public Library, Fraser Valley Regional Library, is at 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road).

Health: Ridge Meadows Hospital (Fraser Health), 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge, provides 24/7 emergency and community hospital services; the Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is in Haney Place Mall, 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Cottonwood MR

items.t: Zoning: City of Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: — the bylaw contains the land-use and development regulations for every property in the city; its residential zones include RS-1, RS-1a, RS-1b, RS-1c, RS-1d, RS-2, RS-3, RST, RT-1, RT-2 and RM-1 to RM-4, and the bylaw schedule gives a minimum lot area of 668 m² for RS-1. Confirm the parcel's own zone schedule before relying on any lot figure.

Suites and added units: one secondary suite per lot, inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area, with a building permit required; eligible single-detached and duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH rules, subject to zoning, bylaw and building code requirements. For a Cottonwood house lot, the suite / SSMUH position — not subdivision into acreage — is the added-value question, and the floodplain exclusion makes the City flood-map check part of the suite diligence.

Kanaka Creek setbacks apply next to the creek corridor, and the suite rule above excludes suites in the Floodplain Area — flood status is therefore a value item on creek-side and low lots, not a formality.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cottonwood MR acreages

items.t: "Cottonwood" is a board name the City does not use: The City of Maple Ridge's neighbourhoods page lists ten named neighbourhoods and Cottonwood is not among them; the City and school district anchor this area by Kanaka Creek and its two elementary schools instead.

The creek through the subdivision is a salmon system with a hatchery: Kanaka Creek Regional Park protects the creek corridor through this part of Maple Ridge, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery on it supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout; the Canyon Trail runs 1.2 km one way from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls and the Riverfront Trails run 3 km one way at the creek oxbow and the Fraser River. Creek-adjacent lots gain the trail system and inherit the setback / slope diligence in the same parcel.

The sample catchment address is the school's own address: The locator run used 11120 234A Street (Kanaka Creek Elementary's own address) and returned Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary (10445 245 Street), while SD42's east zone also runs Garibaldi Secondary (24789 Dewdney Trunk Road) and Thomas Haney Secondary. A Cottonwood listing that names a secondary school without a locator run for that address is ahead of the evidence.

faq.a: Yes — a townhouse strata lot is governed by the same Strata Property Act framework: Form B on resale, mandatory depreciation reports for stratas of 5+ lots, the 10% minimum CRF contribution, and the same bylaw rules.
faq.q: Do strata rules apply to a townhome the same way as a condo?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind you.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Cottonwood townhome?

faq.a: Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC (unlike rental bylaws).
faq.q: Are pets allowed in these complexes?

faq.a: The complexes span 1996 (Hollyhock) to 2020 (Willow & Oak), with The Meadows at Verigin's Ridge's year in conflict between sources (2008 vs 2012). For the 1990s–2000s complexes, the depreciation report is the document that shows upcoming roof, road and envelope work — read it before writing.
faq.q: How old is the stock, and what does that mean for levies?

faq.a: For Willow & Oak, Cottonwood Green, Cottonwood Grove, Maplewood Creek, Hollyhock and The Falls, confirm tenure on title before writing: strata means fees and a Form B; fee-simple means no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.
faq.q: Is a Cottonwood townhouse strata or fee-simple?

faq.a: That line reflects a rental-restriction bylaw, and rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022 — a strata cannot ban long-term rentals by bylaw, though short-term rentals can still be restricted.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Carriage Lane townhouse? The directory says rentals are not allowed.

faq.a: No strata one — Maple Ridge has zero known 55+ strata townhouses. The 55+ townhouse-form community at the sub-area's north edge, St. George's Village, is a co-operative: you buy shares with board approval, not a strata lot, and there is no Form B.
faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse I can buy in Cottonwood?

faq.a: By zone schedule: the bylaw gives a minimum lot area of 668 m² for RS-1, and the other RS variants (RS-1a–RS-1d, RS-2, RS-3) carry their own schedules in Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019. That is house-lot scale — confirm the specific lot's zone before relying on a size claim.

One suite per lot is permitted inside the single detached building, up to 40% of gross floor area, not in the Floodplain Area, and a building permit is required — confirm the lot is outside the mapped floodplain before underwriting rental income.
faq.q: Can a house have a secondary suite?

faq.a: To the south, the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan was adopted January 27, 2026 per the City record (corridor ends at 221 Street) — context, not a Cottonwood entitlement.
faq.q: What plan governs Cottonwood — is there a neighbourhood plan coming?

faq.a: Eligible duplex lots can have up to three, four or six units under the City's rules, subject to zoning, bylaw and servicing conditions — added-unit potential, not a right to split the lot into half-duplex titles.
